puzzles.matchTitle: Vijf minuten dicht, midden op de dag
puzzles.title: Closed for Five Minutes, Right at Noon
puzzles.scenario: Every day at the stroke of noon, a shopkeeper flips his sign to 'closed' for exactly five minutes, then flips it back, while the lights stay on and he never actually leaves the shop.
puzzles.solution: He's simply eating his sandwich behind the counter and hates the idea of customers watching him chew. That's the whole story.
puzzles.hint: What does he need five minutes for, if he doesn't even leave the shop?

puzzles.matchTitle: Een uur per week in een lege opslagbox
puzzles.title: One Hour a Week in an Empty Storage Unit
puzzles.scenario: For a year, a man has rented a storage unit across town where he spends exactly one hour every Sunday, never carrying anything in or out.
puzzles.solution: The unit holds a drum kit he could never play at home without driving the neighbors mad. The storage facility is far enough from houses that no one complains, and packing the kit up and back down each week would eat into his one free hour, so he just leaves it there.
puzzles.hint: What could you do in a locked room that you couldn't do at home, that has nothing to do with belongings?

puzzles.matchTitle: Nooit een vergadering van precies een half uur
puzzles.title: Never a Meeting of Exactly Half an Hour
puzzles.scenario: A project manager schedules every meeting for exactly forty-nine minutes, never thirty, never an hour, and refuses to explain why whenever someone asks.
puzzles.solution: The room-booking system bills by the quarter hour it rounds up to, with a quirk only he ever bothered to work out: forty-nine minutes is the longest a meeting can run without tipping into the pricier bracket. He saves a few euros a week and finds it just a bit too petty to explain to his team.
puzzles.hint: Don't look at the clock in the meeting room — look at the bill that comes after.

puzzles.matchTitle: Altijd de neus naar de uitgang
puzzles.title: Always Nose-Out Toward the Exit
puzzles.scenario: A woman always parks her car nose-out toward the exit, in every spot she's ever used, even in a dead-end driveway where no one would ever need to leave in a hurry.
puzzles.solution: Her father spent years as a dispatcher for the ambulance service and drilled into her that a car ready to pull away can save precious seconds in an emergency. The habit stuck long after the reason behind it faded into the background.
puzzles.hint: Think about who taught her to drive, and what that person did for a living.

puzzles.matchTitle: Regen, elke dag, al een jaar lang
puzzles.title: Still Raining, Every Day for a Year
puzzles.scenario: For a year, a man has texted his sister the exact same three words every morning at eight: 'still raining,' even though he lives somewhere it barely rains, and she always just replies with a thumbs-up.
puzzles.solution: It started as a bet with a friend who forgot about it long ago, to spend a year sending a completely meaningless message. His sister found it so funny and boring after a few weeks that the thumbs-up became a fixed part of their mornings, and now he mostly keeps sending it for her.
puzzles.hint: Don't ask why he started. Ask why he never stopped.

puzzles.matchTitle: Precies een kwartier wachten op hetzelfde gerecht
puzzles.title: Exactly Fifteen Minutes for the Same Meal
puzzles.scenario: A regular at a small diner orders the same dish every day, but always asks the waiter to bring it exactly fifteen minutes later, never sooner, even though the kitchen is known for being fast.
puzzles.solution: He needs to take his blood-sugar medication precisely on time with his first bite. His own schedule is too unpredictable, but the diner's fifteen minutes never are, so he built his routine around the kitchen's reliability instead of his own.
puzzles.hint: What has to happen for him exactly on time, right before he eats?

puzzles.matchTitle: De gevonden-voorwerpenbak die elke vrijdag leeg is
puzzles.title: The Lost-and-Found Box That's Empty Every Friday
puzzles.scenario: At a school, the lost-and-found box is always overflowing with sweaters and lunchboxes by Thursday, but it's completely empty every Friday afternoon, though no one has ever seen anyone clear it out.
puzzles.solution: A teacher goes through it every Friday during her lunch break as a kind of private game: she tries to match each item to the right student from memory and returns everything to their lockers herself, so the box goes into the weekend empty.
puzzles.hint: Who at the school knows the students well enough to return unlabeled things to the right person?

puzzles.matchTitle: Alle straatlantaarns doven tegelijk, tien seconden lang
puzzles.title: Every Streetlight Dims at Once, for Ten Seconds
puzzles.scenario: In a new housing estate, every evening at a slightly different time, all the smart streetlights dim in unison for exactly ten seconds, and the grid operator insists nothing is wrong with the power supply.
puzzles.solution: The lights are wired into a city pilot program: whenever a sensor at the animal shelter down the road detects a stray near the main road, the lights dim briefly as a silent signal to a volunteer group's app, with no siren and no notice to residents. The timing just varies, because animals don't keep a schedule.
puzzles.hint: The signal isn't meant for residents. Who is it for, and what triggers it?
